evidence.quote: 1.3 Scope of Sampling Program The six compounds of concern identified by VTDEC in the letter dated April 8, 2016, are the following.  Perfluorobutanesulfonic acid (PFBS)  Perfluoroheotanoic acid (PFHpA)  Perfluorohexanesulfonic acid (PFHxS)  Perfluorooctanoic acid (PFOA)  Perfluorononanoic acid (PFNA)  Perfluorooctanesulfonic acid (PFOS) Soil and groundwater samples will be submitted for analysis of these six compounds. VTDEC also provided suggested sampling locations and wells in locations of the facility where the potential presence of PFCs was the highest. VTDEC also suggested IBM sample off-site bedrock monitoring wells north, east and west of the former IBM facility. IBM assumes the request to sample off-site bedrock wells w as to establish upgradient and side- gradient “background” groundwater conditions. However, IBM proposes to limit the scope of sampling to within the physical boundaries of the former Site. It is our opinion sufficient information and acreage is available to not only establish upgradient background groundwater conditions, but also large swaths of land are available away from any former potential PFC use areas to establish background conditions for soil. With regards to remedial treatment system effluent, IBM believes the need for this data is premature. The goal of this investigation i s to determine the presence of targeted PFCs in soil and groundwater. Additiona lly, the sediment and surface water sampling performed in October 2016 confirm that PFC-impacted groundwater is not impacting the Winooski River. evidence.quote: 1.0 INTRODUCTION International Business Machines Corporation (IBM) received a letter dated April 8, 2016 from the Vermont Department of Environmental Conservation (VTDEC) requesting IBM sample soil, groundwater and remedial treatment effluent at the former IBM Burlington F acility (see Figure 1) for six polyflourinated compounds (PFCs) , including perfluorooctanesulfonic acid (PFOS) and perfluorooctanoic acid (PFOA). The letter require d IBM submit a Work Plan by April 23, 2016. IBM subsequently retained Golder Associates Inc. (Golder) to prepare this PFC Sampling Work Plan (Work Plan). The purpose of this Work Plan is to determine the presence of the targeted PFCs within soil and groundwater at the former Facility. Included herein is a discussion of the following topics.  The proposed sampling scope of work  Methods for sample collection  Quality assurance/quality control (QA/QC) procedures  Methods for managing investigation derived wastes (IDW)  Schedule  Proposed reporting 1.1 Site Background The site is located in the village of Essex, southeast of the Town of Essex Junction in Chittenden County, Vermont. The site consists of two campuses: the Essex Junction campus and the Williston campus. The main facility is located on the Essex Junction campus, which is bound by County Road 117 to the north and the Winooski River to the east, south, and west (Figure 2). The Williston campus is located east of the main campus and is bound by undeveloped land and the Winooski River to the north, undeveloped land and Redmond Road to the east, undeveloped land to the south, and the Winooski River to the west (Figure 2). The approximately 753 -acre facility was first developed by IBM in 1957. Primary activities at the site initially included the manufacturing of mechanical switches but changed to the manufacture and testing of computer semi-conductors. Numerous and extensive investigations and remedial efforts have been performed at the Site to date. These efforts were initially conducted as part of a RCRA Corrective Action program. However, when IBM divested the facility to Global Foundries, Inc. (Global Foundries) in 2015, the HSWA Permit was essentially transferred to Global Foundries without a Corrective Action Module, and IBM entered into a Consent Order with VTDEC to continue our remedial efforts. 1.2 PFOS
